title: Free-Form Apple Tart with Brown Sugar
changes_from_base: A thin, flat pastry round covered edge to edge with apple slices and brown sugar, instead of a deep case filled with crème pâtissière.
summary: A thin, crisp pastry round covered with apple slices, brown sugar and butter, baked until caramelised at the edges.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
medium Golden Delicious apples (about 600 g), peeled, cored and very thinly sliced

steps.title: Pastry
steps.text: pulse the flour, salt and sugar once or twice. Cut 115 g of the butter into chunks and process it with the yolk for about 10 seconds, until blended.

steps.title: Water
steps.text: tip into the bowl and stir in cold water 1 tbsp at a time; after 3-4 tbsp it should gather into a ball. Wrap and chill 1 h, or freeze 15 min.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Roll or pat the dough into a rough 25 cm round on the paper-lined tray. A rough edge is fine; this tart is meant to look homemade.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: lay the apple slices over the pastry right to the edges in overlapping rows. Sprinkle with the brown sugar and dot with the last 15 g butter, cut into bits. Very thin slices cook quickly and lie flat.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: 20-30 min, until the crust is well browned and the apples are tender. Serve warm or at room temperature with crème fraîche.

tips: A non-stick or lined tray stops the sugary juices sticking.
Chill the shaped base for 10 min if the kitchen is warm.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten the day it is made. Keep leftovers covered at room temperature overnight.
